Minimum Bell-Setting Complexity for Qubit POVM–PVM Separation

General quantum measurements give no extra linear Bell-test power when both parties have only two settings, however many outputs they have; three settings on one side and two on the other are the first possible advantage.

The main new result is arbitrary-finite-output equality of convexified fixed-qubit POVM/PVM behaviors at two inputs per party, completing the minimum-input classification with the credited prior 3×2 advantage; a rational exact witness is supporting rather than first existence.

The exact operational threshold is a strong quantum-information contribution. A later local v2 package reports formally checked principal endpoints and model bridges, materially improving submission readiness if that aligned package is used.

Individual nonprojective measurements can be stronger than projective ones, yet their entire fixed-qubit two-input Bell behavior is reproducible after one common shared-randomness mixture that may change the state.

Bipartite local Hilbert dimension≤2, arbitrary finite input-dependent outputs, shared-randomness convex hulls and linear Bell functionals. No raw-set equality, same-state simulation, operator-level projective simulability, or exact global optimum.
